ai.description: This 20–25 mm frog is olive-brown with dark brown mottling and a distinct white throat. It features a pointed snout, granular skin, and lacks webbing on its fingers and toes.
ai.identificationRemarks: The *Raorchestes silentvalley* is best distinguished by its unique, vibrant bright-yellow iris, which contrasts sharply with the reddish-brown coloration of its body.
ai.habitat: The Silent Valley bush frog inhabits the evergreen forests of the Western Ghats, typically found at elevations between 1,000 and 1,300 meters.
ai.behavior: The Silent Valley bush frog is primarily nocturnal, spending its nights perched on leaves where it actively hunts for small insects.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Raorchestes silentvalley* exhibits direct development, bypassing the tadpole stage. They lay small clutches of terrestrial eggs, with breeding occurring during the monsoon.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Raorchestes silentvalley* is endemic to the Silent Valley National Park in Kerala, India, inhabiting high-elevation evergreen forests in the Western Ghats.
ai.callDescription: The Silent Valley Bush Frog emits a high-pitched, insect-like "tink-tink" call, consisting of rapid, repetitive pulses heard within dense, high-altitude rainforests.
